source.title: Training Dynamics of In-Context Learning in Linear Attention
source.authors: Yedi Zhang; Aaditya K. Singh; Peter E. Latham; Andrew M. Saxe

page_placements.theme: Shape of toy ICL transitions depends on parametrisation, initialisation, task and data size

record.tranche_reason: The study's own results refine how in-context learning develops: the loss can drop once or through multiple stages depending on attention parametrization, rank, and initialization. It does not measure induction-head formation.
record.gate_note: The paper measures in-context linear-regression learning dynamics, not induction heads. It does not test previous-token-head composition, repeated-token copying, or whether induction-head formation coincides with ICL gains. Cited induction-head findings are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study analyses loss dynamics of linear and softmax attention trained on in-context linear regression. It never identifies, measures or intervenes on induction heads, previous-token heads, copying, or token-index loss. Olsson et al. is mentioned only as motivation and an analogy, e.g. abrupt drops 'can reflect the formation of an induction head'. Its results are ICL-loss trajectories, a related but different construct from any version, which all name induction heads.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that linear attention acquires ICL through one abrupt drop when key and query are merged. With separate key and query, it improves progressively through saddle-to-saddle dynamics, implementing in-context principal component regression with a growing number of components. Rank and initialization modulate the plateaus, and the same pattern appears in softmax attention. They make no claims about induction heads.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes gradient-flow training of synthetic linear-attention models on in-context linear regression and includes softmax-attention simulations. It does not use an induction-head detector, token-copying task, or mechanistic head intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The trajectory changes with merged versus separate key/query parametrization, separate key/query rank, initialization scale, and the portion of fixed task vectors.

fits_no_version.finding: ICL loss on in-context linear regression falls in one abrupt drop with merged key-query, but in D staged drops (saddle-to-saddle) with separate key-query. This holds in both linear and softmax attention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether ICL acquisition is a single abrupt transition or multiple stages depends on the attention parametrization (merged versus separate key/query), independent of induction heads.

fits_no_version.finding: Separate key/query rank shortens or removes intermediate plateaus; conspicuous plateaus occur only when a new head's value weight grows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The number of visible ICL loss plateaus depends on key/query rank.

fits_no_version.finding: A larger initialization scale shortens plateaus. At the largest scale the loss decays exponentially (lazy regime) rather than abruptly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The abruptness of ICL acquisition depends on initialization scale (rich versus lazy regime).

fits_no_version.finding: Fixing a portion of task vectors elicits in-weight learning alongside ICL. With 0% fixed tasks, only ICL develops.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The training-data distribution governs whether in-context or in-weight learning develops in linear attention.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267 (2025)
record.problems: The experiments concern synthetic linear-regression tasks and linear-attention models, not natural-language induction-head circuits. Induction-head formation, copying behaviour, and token-index loss are not measured. Several trajectories are presented in figures, and no formal confidence intervals or error estimates are given.

untested.parts: Induction-head appearance coinciding with an ICL gain and a loss bump.
Induction heads' share of ICL in large models.
Induction heads across families, sizes, runs or modalities.
Dependence of induction-head formation or persistence on data and training.
Few-shot task learning through non-induction mechanisms.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V5 and gave a limits_scope label. Both are removed because no row measures induction heads. The paper's only link to induction heads is cited analogy, e.g. intermediate-initialization curves resemble 'induction head emergence in natural language settings'. Relation was reset from tests/T5 to discusses/T6.

versions.untested_parts: Induction-head formation through composition with a previous-token head and the [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying mechanism.
The study does not measure induction heads or token-index loss, so it cannot test whether head formation coincides with the ICL gain or a loss-curve bump.
No large-transformer induction-head contribution to most ICL is measured.
The study does not detect induction behaviour across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
The study tests how setup affects ICL learning dynamics in linear attention, but not whether or when induction heads form, or whether induction-mediated ICL persists.
No few-shot task learning through induction heads versus other mechanisms is compared.
Multiple ICL-learning stages are reported, but induction-head formation itself is not measured as a sequence of sub-steps.

statements.correction: Merged linear and softmax attention: one abrupt loss drop. Separate rank-one linear attention: D abrupt drops. Separate rank-one softmax attention: multiple drops separated by slower training. Increasing initialization shortens plateaus in both linear parametrizations; the largest initialization produces exponential-shaped loss decay associated with lazy learning.
statements.problem: Exactly D drops are stated for separate rank-one linear attention; the softmax result is described only as multiple drops. The initialization result concerns linear attention.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Linear-attention ICL under the tested parametrizations, ranks, initialization scales, and task-vector distributions
reader_labels.reason: The trajectory of ICL learning changes with parametrization, rank, initialization, and task setup: it ranges from one abrupt drop to multiple staged drops or shorter plateaus (R1–R10). The paper does not establish corresponding dependence of induction-head formation.
